name: AKUH's 'Signs, Symptoms and Care' programme one million Karachiites suffering from migraine

content.text: He informed the audience about the common occurrence of headache and said that a number of these patients suffer in silence, since these symptoms are misunderstood as being due to 'stress' or mere pretension. However, only one out of a thousand cases of headaches are likely to be due to a serious problem such as a tumour.

Migraines are a common cause of recurrent headaches, generally seen three times more commonly in women as compared to men. The cause of migraines is unclear, although a number of people have more than one member of the family affected, indicating that there is a genetic inheritance involved. The pain can be on one side of the head or on both sides, and is usually associated with nausea, sometimes vomiting.

Although migraines are not curable, new understandings into their mechanisms of occurrence, and new therapies now ensure that a majority of these patients - if diagnosed correctly and started on the right line of treatment - will have considerable relief in their symptoms over a period of time.

Dr Sonawalla cautioned all patients who have frequent headaches against indiscriminate overuse of painkillers. Recent research has shown that these patients may become victims of MOH, or Medicine Overuse Headaches. In other words, the very medicines which can control headaches, can now lead to headaches. Any patient who requires an almost daily use of painkillers for relief should consult his doctor without delay.

Dr Sonawalla informed the audience that AKUH has recently started a Headache Clinic service that specialises in the management of such problems. It would attempt to offer a high standard of care, and a comprehensive management plan, aimed at providing maximum relief to patients who have to otherwise live in distress.

Dr M. Ehsan Bari, Consultant Neurosurgeon, Department of Surgery spoke on the topic of 'Low Back pain-Sciatica "Indication for Surgery." He said that low back pain is extremely prevalent. Nearly every one at some point has had back pain that interferes with his work, routine daily activities or recreation. Low back pain is one of the commonest causes of sick leaves and disability in young and middle aged people.

Low back pain may reflect nerve or muscle irritation or bone lesions, it may also be caused by degenerative conditions such as arthritis, disc disease or osteoporosis. Sciatica-pain along the large sciatic nerve that runs from the lower back down the back of each leg-is a relatively common form of low back pain and leg pain and is usually caused by pressure on the sciatic nerve from a herniated disc (also referred to as a ruptured disc, pinched nerve etc.)

He pointed out that low back pain can mostly be treated without surgery. But when back pain does not respond to medical therapies, surgery may relieve pain caused by back problems. Spinal surgery for disc disease is usually safe with a success rate of 90-95%.

As part of its outreach programme and societal commitment to create awareness of early diagnosis and timely treatment, AKUH has organised over 200 'Signs, Symptoms and Care' programmes in Karachi, Hyderabad and the UAE, benefiting more than 40,000 people. Similarly, Aga Khan University Hospital's Patient Welfare Programme offers financial assistance to those patients who are unable to afford the medical cost of treatment. In 2005, 73 per cent of all patients treated at AKUH were from low- to middle-income groups. Since the inception of this welfare programme in 1986, over Rs 1.4 billion has been disbursed to more than 250,000 needy patients.

content.description: "Ten per cent of the population suffers from migraine headaches which would amount to more than a million patients in Karachi alone," Dr Aziz Sonawalla said this at a seminar held at Aga Khan University (AKU) Auditorium. Dr Sonawalla who is Consultant Neurologist and Director, Headache Clinic, Section of Neurology, Department of Medicine, AKUH was addressing the "Signs, Symptoms and Care," a public health awareness programme of AKUH.
